# Exercise removal through the generated POSIX wrapper.
# Skip on Windows: the POSIX wrapper is sourced by sh, whose paths differ from $WORK there.
[windows] skip
setup_workspace
exec grove add current
exec grove add nested
exec grove add dirty
exec grove add elsewhere
exec grove add feature-long
exec grove add dashed --name=-dash
exec grove switch shell-init --shell sh
cp stdout $WORK/wrapper.sh

exec sh -e $WORK/remove.sh
stdout 'removal checks passed'
stderr 'uncommitted changes'
! stderr 'cannot delete current worktree'
! exists $WORK/workspace/current
! exists $WORK/workspace/nested
! exists $WORK/workspace/elsewhere
exists $WORK/workspace/feature-long
! exists $WORK/workspace/-dash
exists $WORK/workspace/dirty/untracked

-- remove.sh --
. "$WORK/wrapper.sh"
grove switch current
grove remove current
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace"
test ! -d current

grove switch nested
mkdir -p sub/directory
cd sub/directory
grove remove --force nested
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace"
test ! -d nested

grove switch dirty
printf '%s\n' dirty > untracked
if grove remove dirty; then
    exit 1
else
    removal_status=$?
fi
test "$removal_status" -ne 0
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace/dirty"
test "$GROVE_PREV_WORKTREE" = "$WORK/workspace"
test -f untracked

grove remove elsewhere
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace/dirty"
test ! -d ../elsewhere

grove switch feature-long
grove remove --ignore-missing feature
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace/feature-long"
test -d "$WORK/workspace/feature-long"

grove switch -- -dash
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace/-dash"
grove remove -- -dash
test "$PWD" = "$WORK/workspace"
test ! -d "$WORK/workspace/-dash"
printf '%s\n' 'removal checks passed'
